review_scope: Read-only source and patch inspection at aidream eb98ec1cd23d71cc40807ec2e3e468eb8179a045; no tests, browser, live calls, deployment, or source edits.

supports: The route creates a probe before create_prepared_streaming_response; the latter awaits preparation before returning StreamingResponse, so phase entry is emitted before target response headers.

All explicit awaits in _prepare_resume_conversation are wrapped in probe.run; both legacy standalone_coordinator async entry and exit are enclosed in probe.phase. The probe logs fixed phase/outcome literals, monotonic elapsed time, and a truncated SHA-256 digest of middleware request ID; the route logs response handoff after the streaming response helper returns.

The probe does not itself change request parameters, authentication, organization, model, pool settings, or timeout settings. It rethrows await failures and cancellations; existing cleanup sequence remains visible. No extension wire path is changed.
blockers: Durable app_log rows are not guaranteed while the original await is blocked. AppLogHandler.emit returns early when _sink._guard.active, while _drain_loop sets that thread-local flag across await insert_logs(batch) on the same event-loop thread. Any resumed request that runs during a pending insert emits to logging but its durable row is silently dropped. This invalidates the promised app_log location of an in-flight stall, particularly with concurrent DB/pool trouble. A targeted installed-handler/queue test under pending drain is absent.
limits: Source proves instrumentation placement, not that the original member flow answers or which awaited call caused its 504. No current-server original reproduction or production telemetry was examined.

The 17 focused pass and 28+1 broad result are builder-reported; this lane did not rerun them. The retired DB tenant explanation for the broad podcast_race failure was not independently verified here and remains a gate to resolve, not a waiver.

important: The new marker depends on a sink whose thread-local reentrancy guard spans an async await. Because concurrent application tasks share the event-loop thread, an unrelated drain operation suppresses probe records without notice; this violates nothing-fails-silently for the stated diagnostic outcome. Fix/reuse the sink semantics so the marker survives concurrent drains, then prove the installed handler path with a forced blocked drain and one resume phase.

Current blocked/cancel/failure tests assert caplog records, not AppLogHandler.emit or durable queue presence. The privacy test calls _record_to_row directly. These tests can pass while all diagnostic rows are dropped by emit; they do not force the key telemetry contract.
minor: The outer wrapper emits failed_final or cancelled using last_phase even after that phase completed, so a synchronous validation failure after target_resolve can be attributed to target_resolve. Treat terminal prepare failure as its own fixed phase to avoid falsely implying the last await failed.
verdict_B_doctrine_quality.positive: The patch reuses the existing logging tree and app_log sink, bounds event vocabulary, omits raw ambient identity from app_log rows, and adds an AST census for explicit awaits and async context manager entry/exit.

readiness: NO-GO for source readiness until sink-drop blocker and forcing installed-handler test are addressed. No causal repair or product acceptance inferred.
